record.title: Tan Thanh–Po Chai halts Vietnamese cargo exports during COVID controls
record.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
record.scope: Vietnamese exports through Tan Thanh–Po Chai (Pu Zhai)
record.movement: Vietnam-to-China freight, including fresh agricultural produce.
record.exceptions: Imports into Vietnam and empty-vehicle returns were possible by December 22–23; not a total two-way border closure.
record.enforcement: Contemporary gate official and truckers describe halted exports; first three agricultural export vehicles cleared January 25.
record.relationship: Separate crossing from EA027 Dongxing and R2-EA-006 Hekou; related but not duplicate of three Chi Ma spells.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; unknown endpoints are not extended to 21 October 2026.
record.official_rationale: Strengthen COVID-19 prevention, according to MoIT account of Guangxi decision.
record.context: Earlier December 15 technical interruption is excluded; the new December 18 halt followed a short resumption.
record.uncertainty: Chinese reason was not initially announced to the local official; later ministry report supplies public-health attribution. Reopening remained low-capacity.

historical.duration_note: Calendar-date difference to the stated partial reopening for the specified movement and crossing; not exact hours or universal closure. Eligible only as the calendar gap to first documented Vietnamese agricultural-export passage on January 25; low-capacity partial resumption, not normalization or a two-way closure.

December 18 restart then renewed suspension, consistently dated.

followup_reviews.Researcher: root and verification_recovery, separate original half audits
followup_reviews.Separate challenger: rounds_protocol, separate same-model challenge of both original halves; prior involvement disclosed
followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the deliberate Chinese clearance interruption affecting Vietnamese exports through Tan Thanh–Po Chai. December22–23 inward imports to Vietnam continued while exports remained stopped. Chi Ma counts and reopening are distinct from Tan Thanh. Retain December18 to January25,38calendar days, to three observed agricultural-export vehicles on the first restoration day. Low capacity and later normalization remain separate. The Vietnamese ministry attributes the Chinese suspension to COVID controls; that later attribution is not backdated into every initially unexplained local report. Fresh ministry, VTV, Tuoi Tre and TTXVN bodies were read. VTV overlaps the ministry announcement, and VietnamPlus/Bao Tin Tuc are one TTXVN family. Unrevisited historical details are not newly certified. Retain unlocated export-specific geometry and null coordinates; a shared post name does not establish a two-way full closure or a surveyed marker.
followup_reviews.Challenge verdict: Accepted within the root decision; see frozen challenge
followup_reviews.Challenge finding: Challenge packet SHA-256: c6e6fa17f0d3353c233102eec4583df128ecbb23a0ee9696770f763c8bafc444. Per-question challenge findings remain in that packet.
followup_reviews.Root decision: Accept16full-current-domain assessments with unresolved findings retained and seven guarded native changes: one observed-reopening flag, three Argentine cohort summaries and three phase-specific labels. Retain all dates and numerical durations, all held/incomplete phases, exceptions and unlocated geography. Accept14source-metadata refinements without expanding evidence claims.
